description.content: File transfers now use SFTP (SSH), the WinSCP way: Deskpin connects as the machine's own user and lands straight in their home folder — no admin shares, no C$, no LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy, no drive-redirection dependency, no profile-folder guessing.

The remote pane shows the real remote filesystem with POSIX paths (/), breadcrumbs and a go-to-path bar; browse, drag across the divider or use Send/Get, with live progress, throughput and ETA in the transfer dock (Queue + History), cancel/retry/skip and overwrite Replace/Keep both/Skip.

Works uniformly across Windows, Linux and macOS: Linux/macOS already run SSH; Windows needs the built-in OpenSSH Server enabled once — the machine's right-click "Enable file access" hands you the exact command.
Per-machine SFTP port (default 22) on the Add/Edit dialog. Machines still carry their OS: Remote (RDP) stays disabled for macOS, but file browsing works on all three over SFTP.
Connection state is explicit: a green "SFTP connected" pill when the session is up, a clear "Not connected" overlay with the reason and a Retry button when it isn't.
Security unchanged: the password is revealed from DPAPI only to open the SSH session and is never persisted in plaintext; the generated .rdp still contains no secret.
Also in this line: merged Machines & Files console, Nocturne dark theme, report-a-bug from the Info tab, and real file logging with a 3-second auto-hiding toast.
